deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of Riemann's fragment 'Neue mathematische Principien der Naturphilosophie', section b ('motion which causes the phenomena of light'). Section a (previous page) characterised the gravitational part u of the aether ('Stoff') velocity: curl u = 0, div u = -4π ρ, decay at infinity. This page derives the field equations for the light part w. Section c (next page) combines the two into the laws for the total velocity v.

Setup. The light motion in empty space is taken as a superposition of plane waves. This is justified on the previous page 'by a theorem', i.e. Fourier decomposition. In each plane-wave system the motion is constant along every wave plane. By experience the motion is parallel to the wave plane, and it propagates normal to the plane with a speed c that is the same for all kinds of light.

Step 1 (wave-adapted coordinates). Choose orthonormal coordinates ξ1 normal to the wave planes and ξ2, ξ3 parallel to them. Let w1, w2, w3 be the velocity components along these axes at time t. Constancy on wave planes gives ∂w/∂ξ2 = 0 and ∂w/∂ξ3 = 0 for every component, so w = w(ξ1, t).

Step 2 (transversality, from experience). w1 = 0.

Step 3 (two travelling waves, from experience). w = w' + w''. Here w' is the part travelling toward +ξ1 and w'' the part travelling toward -ξ1, both with speed c.
- The w' part satisfies w'(ξ1 + c dt, t + dt) = w'(ξ1, t). To first order this gives (∂w'/∂t + c ∂w'/∂ξ1) dt = 0.
- Likewise (∂w''/∂t - c ∂w''/∂ξ1) dt = 0.

Step 4 (second order). Differentiate the first-order relations:
- ∂²w'/∂t² = -c ∂²w'/∂ξ1∂t = c² ∂²w'/∂ξ1². The implicit step (mine): apply ∂/∂ξ1 to ∂w'/∂t = -c ∂w'/∂ξ1.
- Similarly ∂²w''/∂t² = c ∂²w''/∂ξ1∂t = c² ∂²w''/∂ξ1².
- Adding the two gives the one-dimensional wave equation ∂²w/∂t² = c² ∂²w/∂ξ1².

Step 5 (symmetrisation). Because w1 = 0 and nothing depends on ξ2 or ξ3, two symmetric equations follow:
- div_ξ w = ∂w1/∂ξ1 + ∂w2/∂ξ2 + ∂w3/∂ξ3 = 0;
- ∂²w/∂t² = c² (∂²w/∂ξ1² + ∂²w/∂ξ2² + ∂²w/∂ξ3²).

Step 6 (back to the original frame). Divergence and Laplacian are invariant under orthogonal changes of Cartesian coordinates. The velocity transforms as a vector, and the equation is linear in it. So in the original coordinates x one gets:
- (1) div w = ∂w1/∂x1 + ∂w2/∂x2 + ∂w3/∂x3 = 0;
- (2) ∂²w_ι/∂t² = c² Δ w_ι.
The marginal note 'w_ι statt w' makes explicit that (2) holds for each component ι.

Step 7 (superposition). These equations hold for every plane wave passing through the point (x1, x2, x3) at time t. Because they are linear, they also hold for the total light motion.

Purpose. The next page combines these with curl u = 0 and Δ(dV) = 0. With v = u + w, it obtains div v = 0 (constant density of the 'Stoff') and □(curl v) = 0. It then builds a Lagrangian unifying gravitation and light. In modern terms, w is a divergence-free vector field obeying the vector wave equation, exactly the form of the source-free Maxwell equations for a transverse field.
errors: No mathematical errors. Each step (first-order transport equations, second-order elimination, symmetrisation, rotational invariance) is correct.

Unstated but standard assumptions: (a) the 'theorem' that any motion is a superposition of plane waves (Fourier analysis), which needs regularity/decay conditions and integrals rather than sums; (b) passing the linear equations through an infinite superposition requires differentiating under the integral sign.

w1 = 0 is taken from experience (transversality of light). Mathematically, div w = 0 only forces ∂w1/∂ξ1 = 0, so a constant longitudinal component would also be allowed. Riemann's physical assumption is stronger than the equation he extracts.
The written equation (2) uses w without an index; the marginal correction 'w_ι statt w' fixes this to a componentwise equation.

results.what: Plane-wave motion propagating both ways with speed c, w = w'(ξ1 - ct) + w''(ξ1 + ct), satisfies the 1D wave equation via the first-order transport equations
results.modern_name: d'Alembert's solution / factorisation of the 1D wave operator

results.what: Transverse plane waves (velocity parallel to the wave plane) give div w = 0 and the 3D vector wave equation; by rotation invariance and superposition this holds for arbitrary light motion
results.modern_name: Transverse (divergence-free) vector wave equation, as for the source-free Maxwell field or an incompressible elastic aether
results.usually_credited_to: Transversality: Fresnel/Young (1817-1821); vector wave equations for the aether: Cauchy, MacCullagh, Green (1830s); electromagnetic form: Maxwell (1865)

deep.surprise_reason: This page belongs to Riemann's 'Neue mathematische Principien der Naturphilosophie', published posthumously in his Werke (1876) and well studied. The mathematics (d'Alembert decomposition, rotational invariance of div and Laplacian, superposition) is routine for the 1850s. The transverse aether equations were standard in elastic-aether theory. Its role in Riemann's unified aether program is already known.

checkable.sympy: x,t,c=symbols('x t c'); f=Function('f'); g=Function('g'); w=f(x-c*t)+g(x+c*t); simplify(diff(w,t,2)-c**2*diff(w,x,2))==0
checkable.asserts: d'Alembert form w'(ξ1-ct)+w''(ξ1+ct) solves the 1D wave equation
First-order transport equations (∂t + c∂ξ1)w'=0 and (∂t - c∂ξ1)w''=0

checkable.sympy: x1,x2,x3=symbols('x1 x2 x3'); n=Matrix([1,2,2])/3; e=Matrix([2,1,-2])/3; s=n.dot(Matrix([x1,x2,x3])); F=Function('F'); W=e*F(s-c*t); simplify(sum(diff(W[i],[x1,x2,x3][i]) for i in range(3)))==0
checkable.asserts: A transverse plane wave (amplitude e ⟂ n) is divergence-free in arbitrary Cartesian coordinates
Each component of an obliquely oriented plane wave satisfies the 3D wave equation, equation (2) in the original frame

transcription_corrections: Marginal note reads 'w_ι statt w' (subscript ι), i.e. equation (2) is meant for each component w_ι, not 'w^ι[?]'.
Last paragraph: 'für jede den Punkt (x1,x2,x3) zur Zeit t durchschreitende ebene Welle'. 'den' is a superscript insertion, so the reading is 'für jede den Punkt ... durchschreitende ebene Welle'.
'Hieraus [-...-] folgt': a struck-out word precedes 'folgt'; content unaffected.
In the first-order equation for w', the manuscript correctly has '+c ∂w'/∂ξ1'; for w'' it has '-c ∂w''/∂ξ1'. Transcription is consistent with the image.
